issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs to bound ∫‖x‖⁴ d|μ_k^τ − π^τ| (integral against the total variation measure) but eq:geo_conv bounds |∫ g d(μ_k^τ − π^τ)| for |g| ≤ V(x) = e^{‖x‖} (integral of g against the signed measure). These are different quantities. Moreover ‖x‖⁴ ≰ e^{‖x‖} for all x (e.g. ‖x‖=4 gives 256 > 54.6), so eq:geo_conv cannot be applied with g(x)=‖x‖⁴ directly. The correct argument uses ∫‖x‖⁴ d|μ−ν| = sup_{|f|≤‖x‖⁴}|∫ f d(μ−ν)| ≤ C‖μ−ν‖_V via ‖x‖⁴ ≤ Ce^{‖x‖}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the incorrect justification with the argument: ∫‖x‖⁴ d|μ_k^τ − π^τ| = sup_{|f|≤‖x‖⁴}|∫ f d(μ_k^τ − π^τ)| ≤ C‖μ_k^τ − π^τ‖_V ≤ CRV(x₀)r^{−k} (using ‖x‖⁴ ≤ Ce^{‖x‖} and the sup-definition of the V-norm). This is a short local fix that preserves and improves the claimed rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proximal-gradient scheme with constant step size $\tau>0$ is geometrically ergodic with respect to the Wasserstein-2 distance, that is, there exist a distribution $\pi^\tau$ on $\R^d$, $c>0$, and $\lambda\in(0,1)$ such that $\Wc_2(\mu_k^\tau,\pi^\tau)\leq c\lambda^k$.

issues.failure_explanation: The contraction step requires τ² − τ/(m+L) ≤ 0, i.e. τ ≤ 1/(m+L) (or τ ≤ 2/(m+L) with the full co-coercivity factor of 2τ). But the stated condition τ² < 1/(m+L) does not imply this for m+L > 1 (e.g. m+L=10 allows τ=0.2 with τ²=0.04<0.1 but τ=0.2>0.1=1/(m+L)). Additionally, the proposition claims geometric ergodicity for all τ>0, which is false: for G=0 (allowed under Ass:F_G) the scheme reduces to X_{k+1}=(1−mτ)X_k+√(2τ)W_k which diverges for τ ≥ 2/m.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the step-size computation in the proof to τ ≤ 2/(m+L) (using the full co-coercivity bound with factor 2τ) or τ ≤ 1/(m+L) (with the paper's weaker bound), and add this step-size restriction to the statements of prop:semi_implicit_fixed_point and prop:added-1. Propagate the corrected bound through lem:bounded_second_moments and (for the step-size aspect) prop:implicit_final_convergence.
issues.overall_effect: Geometric ergodicity of the semi-implicit scheme is unestablished for the claimed full regime τ>0. The LLN result (prop:added-1), uniform second-moment bounds (lem:bounded_second_moments), and the convergence of π^τ to π (prop:implicit_final_convergence, for the step-size aspect) are also affected since they rely on the same contraction bound and on the existence of π^τ.
issues.title: Wrong step-size condition and overclaim in geometric ergodicity of semi-implicit scheme
issues.why_classification: The repair requires correcting the computation and limiting the quantified step-size regime (a limited weakening from all τ>0 to τ ≤ τ₀), which preserves the qualitative result and the practical guarantee of geometric ergodicity for a fixed suitable step size. The excluded large-τ regime is not practically relevant for Langevin discretizations.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For every $f\in L^1(\pi^\tau)$ and the Markov chain $(X_k^\tau)_{k \in \N}$ initialized at $X_0^\tau=x_0$ for any $x_0\in\R^d$ it holds true that \[ \lim\limits_{n\rightarrow \infty}\frac{1}{n}S_n(f)=\E_{\pi^\tau}(f)\quad\text{a.s.} \]
The invariant distributions $\pi^\tau$ satisfy $\Wc_2^2(\pi^\tau,\pi)=\Oc(\tau)$, in particular, $\Wc_2^2(\pi^\tau,\pi)\rightarrow 0$ as $\tau\rightarrow 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion claims the LLN allows computing 'statistics of the target density' (π = e^{−U}/Z). The formal results establish the LLN for π^τ (the invariant distribution of the discretized chain), with E_{π^τ}[f] → (1/n)S_n(f). Since π^τ ≠ π for any τ > 0 (with W_2²(π^τ, π) = O(τ)), the LLN converges to a biased quantity, not to E_π[f]. The same conflation appears in the introduction ('enables sampling from \eqref{eq:target} by averaging across consecutive iterates').

This is a short local prose correction.
issues.overall_effect: The prose overclaims the accuracy of the LLN-based estimator: it suggests exact computation of π-statistics, while the formal guarantee is computation of π^τ-statistics with discretization bias of order √τ in Wasserstein-2 distance.
issues.title: Prose overclaims that LLN computes statistics of target density rather than biased invariant distribution
issues.why_classification: The fix is a short local correction to prose wording that preserves every mathematical claim and the practical message (with an explicit bias caveat). No formal result is affected.
